correctness.rationale: The variety in product_i P Hom(V_{i-1},V_i) imposes f_{i+1}f_i=0 with each arrow nonzero, over C. The generic diagonal one-parameter subgroup has pairwise distinct weights on matrix coordinates in each projective factor, so its fixed tuples consist of matrix units. Consecutive units compose to zero iff their source/target intermediate indices differ. First arrow has d0*d1 choices, and arrow i>1 has (d_{i-1}-1)*d_i choices, totaling d0*d_n product_{i=1}^{n-1} d_i(d_i-1). Additivity of compactly supported Euler characteristic with C* fixed-point localization applies to possibly singular projective variety; projectivity gives ordinary topological Euler characteristic. If an intermediate dimension is one, nonzero adjacent maps cannot compose to zero, so the variety is empty. n=1 gives P^{d0*d1-1} chi=d0*d1. Independently enumerated fixed-point tuples for vectors (1,2,3)->6, (2,3,2)->24, (2,2,2,2)->16, (1,3,3,1)->36, (3,1,2)->0; finite checks corroborate universal C* proof.
